title: docs: update ROADMAP.md for 2026 milestones
body:
## What does this PR do?

Updates `ROADMAP.md` to:
- Mark completed milestones in 2025 Q3 (Podman 5.6 release and Podman 6 HLD).
- Add the 2026 Q1/Q2 roadmap section (Podman 5.7, 5.8, Podman 6.0 planning, Quadlet/machine enhancements).
- Link to the public GitHub Milestones page and issue tracker for live feature tracking.
- Fix minor typographical errors (`importantance` -> `importance`, `RESTFUl` -> `RESTful`).

## Why?

The roadmap had not been updated past 2025 Q3 and left older release milestones unchecked.

Fixes #28288

## Testing

Verified rendered markdown formatting and file links.

comments.body: I don't think this is really appropriate; a lot of the things from the backlog are still ongoing/not complete

Thanks for the feedback. Understood — I see that marking backlog items as completed would be inaccurate while several of them are still ongoing. I'll review the current roadmap and avoid marking ongoing work as complete. Would you prefer that I only update milestones that are definitively completed, or leave the existing backlog items unchanged and make only the necessary 2026 structural updates?
I think we should discuss changes/updates to the roadmap at our community meetings. WDYT? @podman-container-tools/core-maintainers @podman-container-tools/podman-maintainers

As noted on the issue there is nobody who cares to update any of this. Not do I think a file has any useful value with a few lines of nothing...

Proper trackers need to link to existing issues so the status is always visible. And at that point just create github milestones or labels for this and do not bother with this file at all.

The only thing I would like to see is a removal of this file.

Thanks everyone for the clarification. Understood.

Based on the discussion, I'll drop the proposed roadmap updates and instead update #29552 to remove ROADMAP.md, rather than trying to maintain a static roadmap or add links to milestones that aren't currently being used.

Please let me know if you'd prefer the removal to be handled as a separate PR instead.
